candidate.title: FAIRE-seq / Sono-Seq
candidate.scope: Assigned Illumina middle-row architecture for two distinct grouped targets, FAIRE-seq and Sono-Seq. The inspected row labels are FAIRE-seq / Sono-Seq and Formaldehyde-assisted isolation of regulatory elements (FAIRE-Seq) and sonication of cross-linked chromatin (Sono-Seq); its route is Open DNA → Crosslink protein and DNA with formalin → Sonicate → Phenol extract and purify DNA from the aquous phase → DNA. It has one drawn route and no explicit method branch or pooling junction. The left highlighted-linker icon explains the open-chromatin target; neighboring CATCH-IT, MINCE-seq and NOMe-Seq operations belong to other rows. The final blue line denotes recovered genomic DNA; no library adapters, end groups or sequencing instrument are depicted. The full drawn route is retained for FAIRE-seq. Sono-Seq shares fixation and sonication at this schematic level, with its different post-sonication recovery and critical size selection resolved through the poster-associated Auerbach primary paper. Separate downstream routes express alternative method interpretations of the grouped schematic, without asserting a physical sample split. Broad, explicitly paper-supported library/sequencing interfaces explain how the recovered DNA represents chromatin accessibility; unshown routine execution details and comparison assays are excluded.
